Take the relation taught for 'India's Place in World Population' and work with: group_population = 48000, world_population = 1200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share.
Explain in your own words what 'India's Place in World Population' refers to.
questions.a: India holds about 17 per cent of the world's population on a much smaller share of the world's land, making it one of the most populous countries; knowing who lives where, in what numbers and with what characteristics is the work of the census and population studies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India's Place in World Population'.
questions.a: One in every six humans is Indian: population size shapes every plan and resource.

concepts.title: What Determines Population Change: Births, Deaths and Migration

questions.q: Using the method 'What Determines Population Change: Births, Deaths and Migration', work with: birth_rate = 12, death_rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of natural_growth.

Take the relation taught for 'What Determines Population Change: Births, Deaths and Migration' and work with: birth_rate = 25, death_rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of natural_growth.
Explain in your own words what 'What Determines Population Change: Births, Deaths and Migration' refers to.
questions.a: Population size changes through three flows - births add people, deaths remove them, and migration shifts them across borders; the difference between birth rate and death rate gives natural growth, while healthcare, literacy and income steer all three flows.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What Determines Population Change: Births, Deaths and Migration'.
questions.a: Births minus deaths is natural growth; migration adds the human shuffle on top.

concepts.title: Age Composition and the Working-Age Group

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Age Composition and the Working-Age Group' refers to.
questions.a: A population is layered by age: around 27 per cent of Indians are below 15 years, nearly 65 per cent fall in the working-age group of 15 to 59, and the elderly share is rising fast - from about 14 per cent in 2023 toward 26 per cent by 2050 in ageing societies - a shift called population ageing.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Age Composition and the Working-Age Group'.
questions.a: A young majority is a demographic dividend; a swelling elderly share is the coming challenge.

concepts.title: Sex Ratio, Literacy and Regional Patterns

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sex Ratio, Literacy and Regional Patterns' refers to.
questions.a: Population composition also tracks the sex ratio - women were about 48.5 per cent of the population in the most recent count - along with literacy rates that vary sharply among states, and uneven state-wise shares of population shaped by fertility, healthcare and development.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sex Ratio, Literacy and Regional Patterns'.
questions.a: Sex ratio and literacy map the quality of life across India's states.
